input.audience: Primary-school teachers who want more engaging phonics practice.
input.constraints: Do not ask for positive reviews only; paid usage rights and teacher privacy need explicit review.
input.current_ugc_state: A few teacher-led product demos exist; there is no documented rights library or creator brief yet.
input.offer_or_use_case: A teacher chooses a phonics focus and student interest, then creates a decodable reader and matching practice materials.

content_system.trigger: A teacher finishes a useful reader or practice set for a real class need.
content_system.use: Invite a short, optional workflow story with the product proof visible.

content_system.cadence: Brief a small batch before expanding.
content_system.trigger: A teacher agrees to a brief with a defined product proof beat.
content_system.use: Create native vertical clips for paid-social testing.

content_system.cadence: Time the request to the verified use moment.
content_system.trigger: A user reaches a meaningful product-use moment.
content_system.use: Ask every eligible user for an honest review without steering sentiment.

deliverables: Written permission scope for paid usage
do: Show the real product flow and name the phonics focus.
Speak from a real teacher experience and keep the student anonymous.
dont: Do not promise learning gains or use diagnosis-based language.
Do not imply a testimonial or review is independent if it was incentivized.
hook_options: I used the topic they already cared about to start phonics practice.
Here is the small change that made this reading task easier to introduce.
I wanted the practice to feel connected to the student, not generic.
creator_brief.key_message: Show how the selected phonics focus, interest, reader, and practice materials connect in one real workflow.
creator_brief.usage_rights_prompt: Confirm the platforms, territory, duration, paid-ad use, whitelisting, and whether the creator may withdraw permission.

next_14_days: Write and approve one creator brief with rights language.
Collect three permissioned teacher workflow stories.
Cut one proof-led vertical test from an approved story.
Review the first assets for claims, disclosure, accessibility, and product visibility.

paid_ad_plan.disclosure: Add the required paid or sponsored disclosure and confirm the landing-page claim match.
paid_ad_plan.format: Teacher talking-head with product proof insert
paid_ad_plan.hook_test: Test three hooks while holding the proof section constant.
paid_ad_plan.proof_requirement: Show the selected phonics focus, generated reader, and matching practice materials.

review_plan: Ask for an honest review after a documented meaningful-use moment.
Keep positive and negative feedback eligible; do not condition incentives on sentiment.
rights_and_compliance: Record explicit written permission for paid usage separately from organic repost permission.
Have a human review child privacy, teacher privacy, disclosure, and any education-performance claim.
output.strategy_summary: Start with real teacher workflow stories and product-proof clips, then build a small rights-cleared library that can be reused in paid social and review surfaces. Keep claims tied to what each teacher actually experienced.
